eligibility_reason: The paper reports original Facebook URL-share and view analyses of misinformation exposure across the EU and UK from 2017 to 2022. It contains one qualifying reach estimate; other reported percentages describe demographic composition, sample filtering, or cited research.

estimates.measure: share of the European population that saw at least one misinformation story in March 2020
estimates.misinfo_definition: Content fact-checked and labeled as false by an International Fact-Checking Network fact-checker affiliated with Meta
estimates.source_quote: Thepeak is close to .2 on the y-axis, indicating that 20% of the European population saw at least one misinformation story in that month, assuming that each user viewed only one misinformation story.
estimates.notes: The estimate is interpreted from the figure's peak and is conditional on each user viewing only one misinformation story.

considered_but_excluded.why: Gender composition of misinformation exposure, not prevalence.
Gender composition of control-sample exposure, not prevalence.
Share of misinformation URLs with active months after filtering, not a prevalence estimate of misinformation exposure or content.
